Evidence Summary: Google Cloud's Agent Platform enables agents to evaluate context, execute multi-step goals, run code in secure sandboxes, and determine tool usage autonomously. AES uses Claude on Vertex AI to automate auditing without constant monitoring.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Secure sandbox execution and proven autonomous decision-making.

Evidence Summary: Vertex AI Reasoning Engine combines Gemini thinking models with agent frameworks for multi-step reasoning, ReAct loops, and dynamic tool selection. ADK supports planning and task decomposition.
Evaluation Notes: Native Gemini integration and custom Python support. Planning is an advanced capability and not enabled for all agent types by default.

Evidence Summary: Agent Designer and ADK support visual and programmatic orchestration using sequential, parallel, loop, and LLM-driven workflows.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Technical documentation and developer guides
Evaluation Notes: Supports visual flow editing and complex multi-agent architectures.

Evidence Summary: Agent Engine Memory Bank stores and manages long-term user information across sessions. Agent Platform Sessions manage short-term state.
Evaluation Notes: Supports memory extraction, consolidation, contradiction resolution, similarity search, and TTL expiration.

Evidence Summary: Example Store and Gen AI Evaluation Service support performance monitoring and prompt refinement. Vertex AI also supports reinforcement-learning fine-tuning.
Evaluation Notes: Combines evaluation feedback with model-level reinforcement fine-tuning.

Evidence Summary: ADK and the open Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol support heterogeneous agents discovering capabilities, delegating tasks, and collaborating across platforms.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Technical documentation and developer guides
Evaluation Notes: A2A enables cross-platform and cross-vendor agent interoperability.

Evidence Summary: Agent Designer provides natural-language interaction and visual workflows for creating, testing, and connecting agents to sources such as Gmail, Drive, and Jira.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Technical documentation and developer guides
Evaluation Notes: Available across Gemini Enterprise editions and includes CX Agent Studio.

Evidence Summary: Supports Gemini, open-source models through Model Garden/Hugging Face, custom vLLM containers, and third-party models such as Claude, OpenAI, and Mistral.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Technical documentation and developer guides
Evaluation Notes: Gemini has the deepest native support; other models may require LiteLLM or custom vLLM deployment.

Evidence Summary: ADK enables production-ready agents with relatively little code and provides Agent Garden, CLI evaluation, and a visual Web UI for testing.
Evaluation Notes: Supports rapid prototyping through Google AI Studio, Cloud Shell, and local evaluation tools.

Evidence Summary: Agents integrate through MCP, OpenAPI, Apigee API Hub, 100+ Application Integration connectors, and Google Search grounding.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Technical documentation and developer guides
Evaluation Notes: Native MCP proxy support, enterprise connectors, and live grounding.

Evidence Summary: Agents can run on Vertex AI Agent Engine, Cloud Run, GKE, Google Distributed Cloud (air-gapped), or custom infrastructure using Terraform.
Evaluation Notes: Supports managed, serverless, air-gapped, Kubernetes, and infrastructure-as-code deployments.

Evidence Summary: Agent Builder and ADK allow workflows to pause for human approval, preserve execution state, rewind conversations, and enable operator review.
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories; Official product documentation
Evaluation Notes: State checkpoints are maintained automatically during approval pauses.

Evidence Summary: Cloud Logging, Monitoring, Trace, and ADK OpenTelemetry conventions track execution logic, reasoning steps, and tool calls.
Evaluation Notes: Strong tracing and monitoring, but formal feature-attribution explainability is limited.

Evidence Summary: Features include Cloud IAM agent identity, Model Armor, VPC Service Controls, CMEK encryption, and Agent Registry governance.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Technical documentation and developer guides
Evaluation Notes: Provides prompt-injection protection, least-privilege IAM, and audit controls.

Evidence Summary: Managed Agent Runtime automatically scales compute, memory, and sessions. GKE supports horizontal pod autoscaling with GPU/TPU acceleration.
Evaluation Notes: Supports multi-region serverless deployments and high-throughput GKE workloads.

Evidence Summary: Google Cloud provides domain-specific platforms such as CX Agent Studio and documented deployments across finance, real estate, retail, legal, and customer support.
Source Type: Official product documentation; Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Demonstrated adoption across multiple enterprise domains.

Evidence Summary: Google Cloud customer deployments report measurable operational and financial benefits, including AES reducing audit costs by 99% and audit time from 14 days to one hour, Commerzbank reducing administration time by 66%, and Wayfair updating product attributes 4× faster with Vertex AI.
Source Type: Customer case studies and implementation stories
Evaluation Notes: Demonstrates operational value, although reported figures are self-reported by customers.
